en.title: Moksha Patam
en.intro: The old Indian game of snakes and ladders, played as one life. Grow from a baby through childhood and the four ashramas, with a story from the Panchatantra or the Upanishads on every square. Virtues lift you up; vices drag you back down the board, always just before the virtue that heals them, and the years they cost are not given back. The first to land exactly on Moksha, at 105, is liberated; the heavens past it are still the wheel. Tap any square to read it.

hi.title: मोक्ष पटम
hi.intro: साँप-सीढ़ी का पुराना भारतीय खेल, एक जीवन की तरह खेला जाता है। शिशु से बचपन और चारों आश्रमों से होकर बढ़ें, हर खाने पर पंचतंत्र या उपनिषदों की एक कथा है। गुण ऊपर उठाते हैं; दोष आपको बोर्ड पर नीचे खींच लेते हैं, ठीक उस गुण के पास जो उन्हें ठीक करता है, और उनमें गए बरस लौटते नहीं। जो सबसे पहले ठीक १०५ पर मोक्ष पहुँचे, वही मुक्त; उसके पार के स्वर्ग भी संसार का ही चक्र हैं। किसी भी खाने को छूकर उसकी कथा पढ़ें।

JOINS.about: Joining phrases for the life account (docs/NARRATIVE.md §9). Each join goes before a moment and reads on into it, so it ends in a comma or a space. Chosen by how the moment relates to the one before it, first match winning (src/engine/account.js): snake (the years a vice undid; no time passes), a square's own echo, ladder, again (a snake or ladder taken a second time), gap, sameYear or months, then one of then, drawn per life. The fold lines stand in for squares lived a second time.

CAST.about: The cast in the account (docs/NARRATIVE.md §13.3–13.4; src/engine/cast.js). intro is said once, at the end of the moment where a life first meets a member of the cast; call is how a moment calls them by name (the teacher is आनंदजी); family names the parents, who are not given names. returns is the join for the same person returning, one scaffold per member (src/engine/account.js), with the recall of the moment where they were met. The fate lines close the account, one per member met, in the order met: who they were, when they were last seen, and what the life never found out. {who} is the member a line is about, {n} the bare name.
